ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure shows a long solenoid/coil, with a dashed line in the center labeled “Axis of solenoid”, indicating the axis of the solenoid. There are red arrows on the wire, and the current symbol I is marked in several places, indicating that there is current I in the coil. Then reason: The formula for the magnetic field inside an ideal solenoid is B = μ0 n I, where n is the number of turns per unit length, and I is the current through the coil. When the ideal solenoid structure is fixed and n is unchanged, B is directly proportional to I. Therefore, the magnetic field inside the solenoid is directly proportional to the current I.
